claims.text: The starting material is a solid (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy.
Controlled thermomechanical processing can introduce a heterogeneous grain structure into this alloy.
Controlled thermomechanical processing can introduce 3D twin architectures into this alloy.
The proposed heterogeneous grain and twin architecture will increase grain-boundary and twin-boundary density.
Increased grain-boundary and twin-boundary density will provide additional pathways for stress relaxation.
Increased grain-boundary and twin-boundary density will promote crack deflection.
Stress relaxation and crack deflection will increase the alloy's resistance to cracking.
The intervention will increase load-bearing integrity, measured by ultimate tensile strength, by 25% relative to the unchanged alloy.
The intervention will preserve caloric performance, measured by entropy change, relative to the unchanged alloy.
The proposed mechanical and caloric outcomes apply under applied fields from 0 to 5 T.
The proposed mechanical and caloric outcomes apply under pressure fields from 0 to 100 MPa.
The proposed outcomes apply over temperatures from 250 to 350 K.
The proposed outcomes apply during uniaxial tensile loading up to 500 MPa.
Defects introduced by processing or changes in magnetic properties may reduce preservation of caloric performance.

contradictions.description: The central prediction specifies a 25% strength increase, but the experiment only falsifies the hypothesis below a 15% increase. Thus, an observed 15–24% increase would fail the stated quantitative prediction while not meeting the stated falsification criterion.
